body:
We need to have lightweight protocols to transfer links notation representing substitution operations to allow all CRUD operations over TCP/IP as other DBMS systems do.

We must support UTF-8 based text only links notation, and binary version of links notation, that will have number of links in a message/packet, first 256 links should have number of links or ids or addresses 8 bit in size, next we get  16 bit addresses, 32 addresses and 64 bit addresses.

So 0-256 links have 8 bit size.

257-65536 links have 16 bits size and so on.

So for the binary protocol implementation, which should be implemented as another decorator, for both C# and Rust, must be able to be used in the same manner as unicode version of protocol, and be easily switchable between them.

We also should support representation of numbers as defined in links themselves (see how we define numbers in our linksplatform projects on GitHub and so on). Or we should be able to use external references to directly support encoding of unicode sequences if needed.

In that case it will go:

So 0-128 links have 8 bit size.

128-32768 links have 16 bits size and so on.

Also, once we read all links, at the end we can have improved format for storing variable length sequences.

So first section of the protocol is fixed length doublets, and after we recorded all of them we can have additional links with variable lenght.

It goes like this:

size, reference_1, reference_2 and so on (so size defines how to read sequences), as we don't increase size of links, we can reference all links from previous fixed range here.

Each variable link sequences is addressable itself by last link + 1 address or id.

Make sure all these protocols options are optional, and come as decorators in our implementation.

Reuse all the best experience on the topic from other repositories of link-assistant, link-foundation, and linksplatform, so we reuse all the best approaches, if needed to modify these, we can copy the code here, and only later use dependencies, if some components cannot be used as is directly.

We need to collect data related about the issue to this repository, make sure we compile that data to `./docs/case-studies/issue-{id}` folder, and use it to do deep case study analysis (also make sure to search online for additional facts and data), list of each and all requirements from the issue, and propose possible solutions and solution plans for each requirement (we should also check known existing components/libraries, that solve similar problem or can help in solutions).

Please plan and execute everything in this single pull request, you have unlimited time and context, as context auto-compacts and you can continue indefinitely, until each and every requirement fully addressed, and everything is totally done.
title: LINO API or LINKQL over TCP
